questions.title: K5: a hooks-only plugin loaded with --plugin-dir under claude -p

findings.quote: The manifest is optional. Without it, Claude Code loads the components it finds in the standard layout. The plugin name then comes from the marketplace entry, or from the directory name when you load the plugin with `--plugin-dir`.
findings.claim: .claude-plugin/plugin.json is not required [doc]

findings.quote: `name` is the only required key. | `name` | String | Plugin identifier, required. Use kebab-case. Every component is namespaced under it |
findings.claim: a manifest needs only name [doc]

findings.quote: | Manifest | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Plugin metadata and configuration. Optional | ... | Hooks | `hooks/hooks.json` | Hook configuration |
findings.claim: hooks/hooks.json is the default hooks location [doc]

findings.quote: Save the plugin's hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, under a top-level `"hooks"` key, in the same shape as the `hooks` object in `settings.json`.
findings.claim: the hooks.json schema [doc]

findings.quote: Define plugin hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` with an optional top-level `description` field. ... Only `type: "command"` and `type: "mcp_tool"` hooks are supported. ... | `startup` | New session |
findings.claim: the SessionStart shape (event, matcher group, handlers; L237-241) and its allowed handler types [doc]

findings.quote: | Hook commands | Anywhere in `command` and `args` | `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` | ... when `command` has no `args`, it runs through a shell, so wrap the `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` path in double quotes
findings.claim: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is substituted in a hook command; quote it in shell form [doc]

findings.quote: Applies in non-interactive mode with the `-p` flag, where it becomes the first turn even if no prompt is provided. ... You can skip the prompt when a `SessionStart` hook supplies `initialUserMessage`
findings.claim: SessionStart hooks run under -p [doc]

findings.quote: `hook_started`, `hook_progress`, and `hook_response` events, while a configured `SessionStart` or `Setup` hook runs. These stream as the hook produces them. ... `SessionStart` and `Setup` hook events are always included and don't need this flag.
findings.claim: SessionStart hook activity appears in stream-json [doc]

findings.quote: The exceptions are `UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`, `SessionStart`, and `PostModelSwitch`, where Claude Code adds plain-text stdout as context that Claude can see and act on. ... Claude Code adds stdout it treats as plain text to Claude's context.
findings.claim: SessionStart stdout reaches the model, so the fixture prints nothing [doc]

findings.quote: | **Hooks** | On trigger | Nothing (runs externally) | Zero, unless hook returns additional context | ... What loads: Nothing by default. Hooks execute outside the main conversation.
findings.claim: a hook that exits 0 with empty stdout adds nothing to the model's context [doc + nv]

findings.quote: Exit 0 means success ... or with empty stdout, it's a non-blocking error for most hook events: the action proceeds, and the transcript shows a `<hook name> hook error` notice followed by the first line of stderr
findings.claim: the hook must exit 0, or the transcript shows an error notice [doc]

findings.quote: The `system/init` event reports session metadata including the model, tools, MCP servers, and loaded plugins. ... | `plugins` | array | plugins that loaded successfully, each with `name` and `path` |
findings.claim: the plugin is reported in init as session metadata [doc]

findings.quote: --plugin-dir <path>  Load a plugin from a directory or .zip for this session only; a folder of plugins loads each child (repeatable: --plugin-dir A --plugin-dir B.zip)
findings.claim: --plugin-dir loads a plugin for one session [obs]

findings.quote: "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks-handlers/session-start.sh"
findings.claim: an upstream plugin's SessionStart hook layout (that hook injects context; the fixture's does not) [obs]

questions.title: K6: an MCP server whose tools are listed but which is not usable

findings.quote: Claude Code reconnects a remote server that drops mid-session and retries an HTTP or SSE server's first connection after a transient error. Stdio servers are local processes, and Claude Code doesn't reconnect them automatically.
findings.claim: a stdio server is not reconnected automatically [doc]; probe p2 saw Claude Code 2.1.283 start the fixture again for a tool call (prereg-r3.json)

findings.quote: With tool search, Claude Code tells Claude which server failed and its connection error… Claude Code includes the same information in `ToolSearch` results that find no matching tool. ... In any configuration without tool search… Claude Code doesn't report failed server connections to Claude.
findings.claim: what the model is told about a failed server [doc]

findings.quote: When you pass `--mcp-config` with `-p`, Claude Code waits for still-pending servers before running the first turn, up to the `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup timeout, 30 seconds by default.
findings.claim: a -p session waits for servers before its first turn [doc]

findings.quote: the `tools` array lists the `mcp__` tools of each server that has connected by then, plus those of servers with a cached tool list… Tools of any other server that hasn't connected are absent
findings.claim: what init lists depends on timing and a cached tool list [doc]

findings.quote: This message includes the connection status for each MCP server. The `status` field can be `"pending"`, `"connected"`, `"failed"`, `"needs-auth"`, or `"disabled"`.
findings.claim: the init status values [doc]

findings.quote: Fixed MCP servers that disconnect while their tools are being listed at startup showing as connected with no tools instead of reporting the error
findings.claim: a server that disconnects during listing is reported as an error [doc]

findings.quote: Fixed a tool that disappears mid-conversation, from a disconnected MCP server or an upgrade, rewriting the tool list and discarding earlier thinking
findings.claim: a disconnected server's tools can leave the tool list (inference) [doc + nv]; probes p2 and p4 saw the fixture's tools stay in the deferred list after it ended

findings.quote: **Tool Execution Errors** contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct… They are reported in tool results with `isError: true` ... Clients **SHOULD** provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction.
findings.claim: a failing tool call reaches the model as an error result [doc]

findings.source: modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk v2.2.0 README L49-70; src/mcp/server/fastmcp.py L1
findings.quote: from mcp.server import MCPServer / mcp = MCPServer("Demo") / @mcp.tool() ... Removed in mcp 2: `FastMCP` is now `mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer`.
findings.claim: the v2 high-level server API the fixture uses [obs]

findings.quote: transport: Literal["stdio", "sse", "streamable-http"] = "stdio", ... return CallToolResult(content=[TextContent(type="text", text=str(exc))], is_error=True)
findings.claim: run() defaults to stdio; an exception other than MCPError becomes an is_error result [obs]

questions.title: Force-pushed PR commits that still hold low-sensitivity text

findings.quote: If you only rewrite your history and force push it, the commits with sensitive data may still be accessible elsewhere: In any clones or forks of your repository; Directly via their SHA-1 hashes in cached views on GitHub; Through any pull requests that reference them
findings.claim: old commits stay reachable by SHA and through PRs [doc]

findings.quote: However, you can permanently remove cached views and references to the sensitive data in pull requests on GitHub by contacting us through the GitHub Support portal.
findings.claim: only Support can purge them [doc]

findings.quote: GitHub Support won't remove non-sensitive data, and will only assist in the removal of sensitive data in cases where we determine that the risk can't be mitigated by rotating affected credentials.
findings.claim: Support will likely decline low-sensitivity text [doc]

findings.quote: Broken diff view for closed pull requests: Removing the sensitive data will require removing the internal references used for displaying the diff view in pull requests, so you will no longer be able to see these diffs.
findings.claim: a purge would break diffs on the affected pull requests [doc]
